findings.problem: status is a raw String instead of a domain enum, allowing arbitrary invalid values like "foo", "", or "sent" set without corresponding lifecycle updates
findings.failure_mode: callers construct or mutate ShardWorkflow with an illegal status string that has no corresponding typestate transition, producing irrecoverable invalid domain state
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with an enum `pub enum ShardStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }` and make all construction go through smart constructors that enforce the invariant

findings.problem: Lifecycle boolean `is_validated` is independent of `status: String` and `is_sent: bool`, creating impossible-to-enforce invariant that these booleans must stay consistent with status
findings.failure_mode: Any combination of is_validated/is_sent/status is legally constructible, including sent-without-validated, validated-then-invalidated, or double-sent states that the type system cannot prevent
findings.fix: Encode lifecycle as a single enum with explicit variants (e.g. `Pending`, `Validated`, `Sent`) so only one lifecycle stage exists at a time; remove separate booleans

findings.problem: Lifecycle boolean `is_sent` is independent of status and is_validated, creating the same invariant enforcement problem
findings.failure_mode: Caller can set is_sent=true while status remains "pending", producing a shard that is semantically sent but appears pending to all observers
findings.fix: Merge into the typestate enum so `Sent` is a single variant that implies both sent state and any associated data

findings.problem: Optional lifecycle timestamp is a standalone field, not owned by the lifecycle variant that needs it. It can be Some while is_sent=false, or None while is_sent=true
findings.failure_mode: sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some(u64) when the shard was never actually sent, or None when is_sent=true, creating inconsistent observation and silent data loss
findings.fix: Move timestamp into the enum variant: e.g. `Sent { sent_at: u64 }` so the timestamp is present only when the shard is in the Sent state

findings.problem: ID is a raw String primitive with no domain guarantees—no non-empty check, no format validation, no protection against mixing with other String fields
findings.failure_mode: Empty string, whitespace-only, or malformed IDs are accepted at the type level, and the compiler cannot distinguish ShardWorkflow.id from any other String parameter
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct ShardId(String)` or `pub struct ShardId(&'static str)` with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and returns a typed error

findings.construct: pub fn mark_sent(mut item: ShardWorkflow) -> ShardWorkflow
findings.problem: mark_sent takes the full struct by value and mutates status string and is_sent boolean independently. No typestate guard prevents calling mark_sent on an already-sent shard, on an invalid shard, or multiple times
findings.failure_mode: Idempotency violation—mark_sent can be called repeatedly, each time overwriting status to "sent" and setting is_sent=true. No validation that the shard was in a valid pre-sent state (e.g. Validated) before transition
findings.fix: Accept a typed pre-sent state (e.g. `ShardValidated`) and return `ShardSent`. Each transition function consumes its specific input typestate and produces the next, making illegal transitions compile-errors

findings.problem: All fields are public with no smart constructor or parse boundary. Raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly
findings.failure_mode: Every caller can create a ShardWorkflow with status="", is_validated=true, is_sent=true, sent_at_epoch_ms=None—a fully constructed but semantically impossible shard that passes all compile-time checks
findings.fix: Make all fields private, provide `ShardWorkflow::new(...)` or `ShardWorkflow::from_pending(...)` smart constructors that validate invariants and return typed errors, and use private fields only

findings.problem: Hard-coded string literal assignment to status bypasses any enum discipline. If status is later converted to an enum, this code will not compile; if kept as String, the literal is invisible to the type system
findings.failure_mode: Typos in the status string (e.g. "sant" vs "sent") compile silently and produce undetectable domain errors
findings.fix: Replace with enum variant assignment: `item.status = ShardStatus::Sent`

residual_risk: Static review only, no commands run. The crate compiles as-is but violates multiple absolute Holzman Rust laws: raw-primitive domain state (String id, String status), lifecycle booleans (is_validated, is_sent) instead of typestates, optional lifecycle data outside its owning variant, no smart constructors or parse boundary, mutable struct with independent field mutation, and no benchmark/profiler/clippy evidence. All findings are BLOCKERs that must be repaired before delivery.
